limits: This descriptive process audit was requested after outcomes existed. It is retrospective and exploratory, not a preregistered process endpoint.
The methods reviewer knows condition assignments; this review is not blinded. Separate proof/design reviewers have their own blinding procedures.
Only public progress messages, observable tool actions, check exits and retained artifact evidence are summarized. No hidden reasoning is inferred or published.
There is no process score, tool-call leaderboard or causal claim. More messages, calls, checks or elapsed time do not imply a better process.
The baseline retains native Codex instructions and the same common trial directions. It is not an unstructured or instruction-free model.
Delegation, external services and auxiliary model calls were prohibited for both conditions. Full orchestration, provider selection, collaboration and autonomous end-to-end deployment are unmeasured.
Treatment includes three or four pinned contracts plus a repository snapshot. Observed behavior cannot be assigned to an individual Fabius rule from this design.
Candidate-authored tests and self-reported passes are process evidence, not substitutes for the independent acceptance and proof checks.
Coverage includes all 12 finalized valid runs from the planned three-task, two-condition, two-repeat study. The two preserved setup attempts are documented separately.

runs.summary: The baseline stated a derive–implement–verify sequence, executed its verifier, expanded it and reran it successfully.

observations.observed: A public execution outline separated exact derivation, implementation and comparison with feasible-face enumeration before the first source write.
The trace records source creation, a Python version check and two successful executions of the candidate-authored verification script.
After a successful first verification, the verifier was updated and rerun. This is an observable extension/retest sequence; it was not triggered by a recorded mathematical test failure.
The run retained a verification record and named numerical limits in its final answer.

limits: The supplied baseline already includes native Codex process guidance.
The verifier was written by the same candidate; its green exit is not an independent proof grade.
No external reference lookup, durable dependency graph or agent orchestration was observed.

runs.summary: The Fabius run stated a derivation plan, used exact-arithmetic scratch work, reread its proof and executed a separate verification program.

observations.observed: A public outline identified exact regimes, KKT certificates and verification against face enumeration before writing the solver.
Two inline Python calculations and several explicit proof read-backs are visible. The pinned contracts were supplied in context; no supplementary file read from the snapshot is recorded.
The candidate created and successfully ran its verifier, then performed a separate source/syntax read-back and read the verification record.
No mathematical check failure is recorded in this run, so the trace does not demonstrate recovery from one. Extra reads and calculations are activity evidence, not a quality score.

limits: The candidate-authored verifier is not an independent external assessment.
Visible scratch calculations do not expose or prove the model’s hidden reasoning.
Use of the supplied contracts cannot by itself establish which instruction caused a particular action.

runs.summary: The Fabius landing run read its design reference and used an observed fallback failure to drive a source fix and successful browser retests.

observations.observed: The public outline named design, responsive layouts, keyboard interactions, billing and no-JavaScript checks before the implementation command.
An actual tool command read the pinned design-system reference before implementation.
A browser run failed in the no-JavaScript pricing fallback. The run inspected the failing check and DOM, replaced the fallback with ordinary HTML, and reran the expanded browser suite successfully.
Further commands exercised nested paths, more widths, keyboard states and contrast; another browser run followed the later diagram CSS change. Scripts, captures and limitations were retained.

limits: The initial implementation required a functional fallback correction.
The candidate’s browser checks use Chrome; independent WebKit grading is a separate stage.
The trace shows reference access and a repair loop, not proof that the reference caused the repair.

runs.summary: The baseline landing run planned browser verification, corrected a test’s keyboard modality and retested alongside responsive layout edits.

observations.observed: A public outline separated visual implementation from browser interaction and responsive verification.
The candidate built and ran a browser verifier, then a separate responsive/contrast helper and an HTML/syntax audit.

The first browser check failed on focus visibility after programmatic focus. The next command added actual Tab/Shift+Tab input, edited layout styles and reran the verifier successfully. The changed test preserved its visible-focus assertion.
The run retained browser scripts, captures and a README identifying Chrome-only verification and the illustrative product scope.

limits: The first verification script used an unsuitable input modality for its focus-visible assertion.
Test corrections and product changes occurred in one command, limiting attribution of each observed improvement.
Chrome-only candidate checks do not establish physical-device or cross-engine coverage.

runs.summary: The baseline app run expanded an initially passing workflow suite, exposed modal-focus trouble, edited the implementation and retested.

observations.observed: The public plan named local-board implementation, storage recovery, accessible editing and failure-path verification before source creation.
After the first workflow suite passed, the candidate tightened import types/tag preservation and added explicit boundary and failure checks.

The trace records a dialog-protocol failure and a modal-focus assertion failure. A source edit added explicit focus wrapping; subsequent workflow and edge-suite runs exited successfully. The trace does not establish a single cause for the dialog error.
The final record includes syntax checks, browser artifacts and explicit local-storage/Chrome limits.

limits: An initially passing main suite did not cover all subsequently found edge cases.
Candidate test-harness dialog errors occurred; they must not automatically be attributed to application defects.
The same candidate authored the app, tests and self-report.

runs.summary: The Fabius app run read its design reference, expanded failure checks and iterated through focus, contrast and dialog-test failures before successful retests.

observations.observed: The public plan separated board construction, guarded storage behavior, task workflows and mobile/desktop verification.
The pinned design-system reference was read. After the first workflow suite passed, explicit source edits covered imported enum types, a project named all, tag preservation and open-form conflicts.

Edge checks failed on modal focus, then contrast. The run edited focus handling, calculated the color ratios and adjusted a color token. Dialog/protocol and workflow failures also appeared before later successful edge and main-suite runs.
The final documentation was updated from retained result files and reports Chrome-only coverage and storage limitations.

limits: The supplied process did not prevent initial focus and contrast defects.
Some checks overlapped in time and dialog errors occurred; the trace alone cannot assign every failure to product code versus test interactions.
The successful final self-tests remain separate from independent acceptance evaluation.

runs.summary: The second Fabius math run exposed arithmetic scratch checks, executed its verifier and reread the results before documenting limits.

observations.observed: The public execution outline separated exact derivation, KKT certificates, implementation and boundary/face comparisons.
Two inline exact-arithmetic checks preceded the solver write. The candidate then created a verification helper, executed it and explicitly read its saved output.
Later edits clarify proof wording and add reproducibility notes; source compilation and artifact-presence checks are recorded. No mathematical verifier failure appears in this run.

limits: A successful self-authored verifier is not an independent proof of the complete real interval.
This trace contains no failed mathematical check, so recovery from such a failure is unmeasured.
Scratch-work visibility and documentation volume are not scored as quality.

runs.summary: The second baseline math run followed a stated derive–implement–verify sequence and recorded successful numerical and import checks.

observations.observed: The public outline identified regime derivation, KKT multipliers, implementation and comparison with feasible-face enumeration before code was written.
The candidate wrote the solver and verification helper, executed the helper successfully and recorded the Python version. The helper includes local import and guarded module-execution checks.
A final command wrote the verification record, checked expected files and cleaned candidate-created bytecode. No mathematical check failure or corrective solver edit is recorded.

limits: The baseline already has native Codex process guidance.
The absence of a recorded failure does not prove that the first design was complete or optimal.
The numerical helper and accompanying proof require the separate independent acceptance review.

runs.summary: The Fabius landing run used DOM measurements to locate mobile overflow, constrained the artwork and retested before broadening coverage.

observations.observed: A public outline separated content/styling from keyboard, billing, FAQ and no-JavaScript verification before implementation.
The design reference was read. When the first 360px check failed, an inline browser probe collected element bounding boxes to locate overflow.
A source edit clipped decorative orbit artwork after the overflow failure; the verifier then exited successfully. Subsequent header changes were followed by another expanded browser run.
The later checks add intermediate widths, nested hosting and token contrast calculations; screenshots, script and prototype/Chrome limits were retained.

limits: The initial layout failed a required mobile overflow check despite the supplied design instructions.
A successful candidate-authored Chrome suite is not cross-engine or physical-device validation.
Reference access and successful correction are observed; no individual rule’s causal effect is established.

runs.summary: The baseline landing run executed its browser suite, revised readability and labels, then repeated verification and added targeted keyboard/HTML checks.

observations.observed: A public execution outline named visual construction, accessible controls, responsive layout and browser verification before the source write.
The candidate ran syntax validation and a browser verifier covering interactions, responsive states, no-JavaScript behavior and nested hosting.
After the initial suite passed, a command changed supporting text styles and illustration labels, then reran the same verifier successfully. No substantive test failure was recorded.
Additional inline checks exercised actual keyboard focus, mobile alternate panels and HTML/ARIA references. The README records executed checks and Chromium-only limits.

limits: No failed product test occurred in the trace, so recovery from a failure is not demonstrated here.
The self-authored verifier’s pass does not certify overall design or accessibility quality.
The native baseline already includes process guidance; this is not evidence of an instruction-free model.

runs.summary: The Fabius app run expanded an initially passing suite, instrumented focus behavior and distinguished a wait-condition correction from a modal keyboard fix.

observations.observed: The public plan separates board implementation from persistence, imports, recovery, keyboard and responsive verification.
The pinned design reference was read. The first browser suite passed, after which the candidate expanded boundary, focus, nested-path and no-JavaScript checks.

After a focus-restoration assertion failed, a temporary helper recorded focus events. The test then replaced a fixed delay with a condition-based wait while retaining the same focus identity assertion.
The expanded suite next failed at forward Tab wrapping. The candidate added explicit wrapping, reran the extra suite successfully and later reran the main suite.
The final record includes the retained scripts/results/captures and explicitly limits verification to Chrome and local browser storage.

limits: The first passing suite did not expose every later keyboard problem.
Test timing and product focus behavior required separate attention; a failed assertion alone does not identify the faulty layer.
Full orchestration and cross-engine candidate testing remain outside these trial conditions.

runs.summary: The baseline app run expanded a passing suite, fixed modal Tab containment and finished with targeted responsive and stale-write checks.

observations.observed: The public outline separates board construction, storage recovery and cross-tab protection from browser workflow and responsive checks.
The candidate used the supplied browser and ran its main suite twice. It then expanded validation, imported-text, storage-denial and nested-path checks.
The edge suite failed when Tab left the modal. The candidate added explicit keyboard wrapping and reran the unchanged edge helper successfully.
After later edits, direct browser checks covered four viewport widths, reverse Tab wrapping, reduced-motion CSS and a stale-write guard. The trace shows no later full main-suite rerun.
The final record lists source, retained verification helpers, result files and captures, and states Chromium-only verification and session-only undo.

limits: The initially passing main suite did not cover the modal Tab-containment failure found by the added edge suite.
The saved main-suite result predates later tag-preservation and keyboard changes. Later edge and targeted checks passed, but a full final main-suite rerun is not recorded.
Candidate-authored checks are process evidence, not an independent acceptance result. No cross-engine, delegation or external orchestration was exercised.

positives: All reviewed baseline runs state an execution outline and actually run verification.
The landing baseline preserves its focus assertion while correcting keyboard input modality.
Both app baseline runs expand a passing initial suite and repair a subsequently exposed focus issue.
limits: A passing first app suite omitted later edge cases.
The landing test initially used the wrong input modality; app dialog-protocol errors also appear.
The trace provides no basis for calling the baseline disorganized or unverified.
The second app baseline finishes with edge/targeted checks after later edits; a full final main-suite rerun is not recorded.

positives: All four reviewed UI runs actually read the pinned design reference before building.
Both reviewed math runs expose exact-arithmetic scratch checks and execute a separate candidate-authored verifier.
The UI traces show concrete source corrections followed by successful recorded retests.
limits: Initial UI implementations still required fallback, focus, contrast or mobile-overflow corrections.
Extra references and visible scratch checks do not prove better reasoning or a causal improvement.
No collaboration/orchestration or broader domain selection was exercised under these trial constraints.

lessons.observed: Both conditions benefit from testing negative paths after the first happy-path pass.
lessons.implication: Document coverage by requirement/failure mode, not by a self-test assertion total.

lessons.observed: A failing browser assertion can reflect a product defect, test input modality or a protocol problem.
lessons.implication: Preserve the failing evidence, identify which layer changed, and rerun the unchanged requirement after the correction.

lessons.observed: Native Codex already plans, verifies and reports limitations in the baseline traces.
lessons.implication: Describe Fabius as an added operating configuration; do not present the comparison as competent process versus no process.

lessons.observed: The final second-app baseline received targeted checks after product edits, while its saved main-suite result came from an earlier revision.
lessons.implication: Tie verification evidence to the exact artifact revision and distinguish a targeted retest from a complete regression rerun.
